Displaced native {{ncog|enm|deme}} (from {{noncog|ang|dēma|t=judge}}) and {{m|enm|demere}} (from {{ncog|ang|dēmere|t=judge}}), see also {{m|en|deemer}}, {{m|en|deemster}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|public judicial official}} A public [[official]] whose duty it is to [[administer]] the [[law]], especially by [[presiding]] over [[trial]]s and [[render]]ing [[judgment]]s; a [[justice]]. #: {{syn|en|magistrate|q1=now usually of low rank|justice|q2=now usually of high rank|justiciar|justiciary|q4=historic, of high rank|;|chief justice|Chief Justiciar|Capital Essayes|chapter=Of Judicature|passage=The parts of a '''judge''' in hearing are four: to direct the evidence; to moderate length, repetition, or impertinency of speech; to recapitulate, select, and collate the material points of that which hath been said; and to give the rule or sentence.}} # A [[person]] who [[decide]]s the [[fate]] of someone or something that has been [[call]]ed into [[question]]. # A person [[officiate|officiating]] at a [[sports]] [[event]], a [[contest]], or similar; [[referee]]. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:match official}} #: {{ux|en|At a boxing match, the decision of the '''judges''' is final.}} # A person who [[evaluate]]s something or forms an [[opinion]]. #: {{syn|en|deemer|deemster}} #: {{ux|en|She is a good '''judge''' of wine.}} #: {{ux|en|They say he is a poor '''judge''' of character considering all the unreliable friends he has made.}} # {{lb|en|historical|biblical}} A [[shophet]], a [[temporary]] [[leader]] [[appoint]]ed in times of [[crisis]] in [[ancient]] [[Israel]]. =====Usage notes===== * For information about the usage of ''judge'' versus {{m|en|referee}} and {{m|en|umpire}}, see [[referee#Usage notes|usage notes at ''referee'']]. Partly displaced native {{m|en|deem}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To sit in [[judgment]] on; to [[pass]] [[sentence]] on (a person or matter). #: {{syn|en|rule on|try|Thesaurus:adjudicate}} #: {{ux|en|A higher power will '''judge''' you after you are dead.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To sit in judgment, to act as judge. #: {{syn|en|adjudicate|make a decision|Thesaurus:decide|Thesaurus:sit in judgement}} #: {{ux|en|Justices in this country '''judge''' without appeal.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[judicially]] [[rule]] or [[determine]]. # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[sentence]] to [[punishment]], to [[judicially]] [[condemn]]. #: {{syn|en|deem|sentence|Thesaurus:convict}} #: {{ux|en|He was '''judged''' to die for his crimes.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[award]] [[judicially]]; to [[adjudge]]. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[form]] an [[opinion]] on; to [[appraise]]. #: {{syn|en|evaluate|rate|Thesaurus:appraise}} #: {{ux|en|I '''judge''' a man’s character by the cut of his suit.}} #* {{circa|1921}}, {{w|Michael Collins (Irish leader)|Michael Collins}}, after the {{w|Anglo-Irish Treaty}}: # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[constitute]] a [[fitting]] [[appraisal]] or [[criterion]] of; to provide a [[basis]] for forming an opinion on. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=ii|page=25|passage=Noble and milde this Perſean ſeemes to be,
If outward habit '''Iudge''' the inward man.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[arbitrate]]; to pass [[opinion]] on something, especially to [[settle]] a [[dispute]] etc. #: {{ux|en|We cannot both be right: you must '''judge''' between us.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To have as an opinion; to [[consider]], [[suppose]]. #: {{syn|en|hold|[[regard]] as|Thesaurus:deem}} #: {{ux|en|I '''judge''' it safe to leave the house once again.}} #: {{ux|en|I've been '''judge'''d to have the best qualifications.}} #: {{ux|en|A merit good is a commodity or service that it is '''judged''' an individual or society should have.}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To form an opinion; to [[infer]]. #: {{ux|en|I '''judge''' from the sky that it might rain later.}} #: {{ux|en|However I have the mirror positioned, I can't '''judge''' where the back of the car is.}} #: {{ux|en|We can't always '''judge''' people's ages just by their voices.}} #* {{RQ:Twain Huckleberry Finn|8 |passage=THE sun was up so high when I waked that I '''judged''' it was after eight o'clock.}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[criticize]] or [[label]] another person or thing; to be [[judgmental]] toward. #* {{quote-song|en|year=1993|author=w:Aerosmith|title=w:Livin' on the Edge |passage=There's something wrong with the world today; the light bulb's getting dim.
There's meltdown in the sky.
If you can '''judge''' a wise man by the color of his skin,
Mister, you're a better man than I}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[govern]] as {{w|biblical judges|biblical judge}} or [[shophet]] (over some [[jurisdiction]]). #* {{RQ:KJV|Judges|10|3||And after him aroſe Iair a Gileadite, and '''iudged''' Iſrael twentie and two yeeres.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Judges|12|11|passage=And after him, Elon, a Zebulonite iudged Israel, and he '''iudged''' Israel ten yeeres.}}
